## About the project

PyCPT Tutorial connects readable climate-forecast stories with executed notebooks
and traceable data to teach the use of PyCPT. CPT is the underlying engine for
PyCPT model fitting; this is not a standalone CPT installation or operation guide.
Its first case examines seasonal rainfall forecasts over
Indonesia across twelve windows centred on 2023. Seasonal and subseasonal topics
are part of the project's broader scope; only completed, verified material is
presented as an available case.

The current case is complete as a reproducible tutorial. Physical interpretation
of fitted patterns, longer independent validation and probability reliability
remain separate research questions. See [methods and limitations](methods.qmd)
for the evidence supporting the published comparisons.

The source is maintained in the [pycpt-tutorial repository](https://github.com/bennyistanto/pycpt-tutorial).
This is a tutorial project, rather than a replacement for upstream software documentation.

## Upstream software and teaching references

- [PyCPT source and documentation](https://github.com/iri-pycpt/pycpt)
- [IRI PyCPT example notebooks](https://github.com/iri-pycpt/notebooks)
- [IRI teaching reference: CPT, calibration and cross-validation](https://iri.columbia.edu/~awr/pycpt/seasonal-jupyterbook/html_2sep2023/cpt.html)
- [CPT help](https://cptplus.org/Help/CPT_use_contents.html)
- [Quarto](https://quarto.org/), used to publish the story, notebook and guides

The executed case and its recorded configuration determine the behavior described
here. The [reader guide](start.qmd) separates browser reading, offline analysis,
optional PyCPT fitting and conditional data-access requirements.

## Data and boundary provenance

The case uses CFSv2 model rainfall and CHIRPS3 observations. Country and province
boundary files supplied for the project provide map context and regional assignments.
The analysis and simplified display boundaries have separate provenance records.

| Material | Source record |
| --- | --- |
| Packaged case inputs, calendars and hashes | [Data provenance](../data/provenance.json) |
| Country, province and neighbouring-country map overlays | [Display-boundary provenance](../data/boundaries/provenance.json) |
| Native province assignments, support and residual | [Province-analysis provenance](../data/regions/provenance.json) |
| Browser-readable chart and map inputs | [Interactive-data provenance](../assets/story/provenance.json) |

## Citation and reuse

When referring to this work, identify **PyCPT Tutorial**, the case title
**Twelve seasons over Indonesia**, the repository revision you used and your
access date. Credit the upstream software and underlying data sources as appropriate.
The [source repository](https://github.com/bennyistanto/pycpt-tutorial) records revisions.

The repository includes a **Mozilla Public License 2.0**
[license file](https://github.com/bennyistanto/pycpt-tutorial/blob/main/LICENSE).
Upstream software and third-party data or boundaries have their own source terms;
the provenance links above identify the supplied material. No additional license
is introduced by this website layout.

## Questions, corrections and contributions

[Report an issue in the repository](https://github.com/bennyistanto/pycpt-tutorial/issues).
Include the page or notebook cell, the selected season/metric/period if relevant,
and what you expected to see. For execution problems, include the software
versions and a concise error message; keep credentials and private paths out of
public reports.

For an explanation of the story/notebook approach, begin with the
[reader guide](start.qmd). For runnable inputs and environment instructions,
use [setup and downloads](reproduce.qmd).
